_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader). Municipal-tier population-priority push, 2026-08-13 (AF/G.18), round 2 of 10. Ethiopia — 2nd-highest-population country. Ethiopia has no ordinary municipal tier; instead it has two federally-chartered city administrations (Addis Ababa, Dire Dawa) that sit alongside, not beneath, the 11 regional states. This file documents that structure and resolves this branch's own open question `et-proc-1365-addis-applicability-unverified` (af-grok-municipal-batch2.json) about whether Proclamation 1365/2025 names Addis Ababa specifically — it does.

reports.title: 2016 Fiscal Year (2023/24) Federal Government Budget Proclamation No. 1297/2023
reports.publisher: House of Peoples' Representatives, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
reports.description: Ethiopia's federal budget proclamation, published in Federal Negarit Gazette No. 38 (14 September 2023) and directly downloaded from the Ministry of Justice's own site. Article 7 ('Subsidies to Regions') lists Addis Ababa City Government and Dire Dawa Administration as separate, numbered line items structurally parallel to the 11 regional states, not nested under them: "441 Addis Ababa City Government 5,254,541,684 ... 442 Dire Dawa Administration 1,837,611,323", alongside "431 The State of Tigray 12,591,813,948 ... 439 The State of the Harari People 1,587,027,961". Sub-article 7.10 breaks Addis Ababa's own subsidy into External Loan (5,215,724,800 Birr) and External Assistance (38,816,884 Birr); sub-article 7.11 breaks Dire Dawa's into Domestic Source (1,811,501,996 Birr) and External Assistance (26,109,327 Birr). Note an asymmetry: Article 8 ('Support for Achievement of SDGs') lists a Dire Dawa line (8.10) but no separate Addis Ababa line, unlike Article 7. This is a fixed itemized appropriation, not a percentage formula.
reports.cadence_note: Annual federal budget proclamation; this edition covers Ethiopian FY2016 (Gregorian 2023/24).

reports.title: Addis Ababa City Council 2016 E.C. (2023/24) Approved Budget Announcement
reports.publisher: Addis Ababa City Administration Bureau of Finance
reports.description: Addis Ababa City Administration Bureau of Finance's own website reports a specific approved city budget with a real breakdown: "The Addis Ababa City Council approved a 2016 budget of 140,291,550,064.00 Birr", broken down as Regular city expenses (23,498,446,197.00 Birr), Capital expenditure (69,336,835,072.00 Birr), Reserve funds (5,300,000,000.00 Birr), Sub-cities regular expenses (33,498,495,001.00 Birr), Sub-cities capital expenditure (8,657,773,794.00 Birr) — quoted as "a significant 40% growth compared to the previous year" by Finance Office head Abdir Qadir Redwan. CAVEAT: direct HTTP access to this URL failed repeatedly (TLS connection reset) via direct fetch tooling; this content was retrieved only through an AI-summarizing fetch tool, not independently re-verified against raw HTML — matching this branch's existing practice of flagging AI-summarized-only sourcing distinctly (cf. Liberia's LISGIS pricestats.php page). The article does not state whether "2016" is the Ethiopian or Gregorian calendar year, nor give a proclamation number.
reports.cadence_note: Annual city budget; this is the most recent approved figure found, verification-limited per the caveat above.

reports.title: Proclamation No. 1250/2021 — A System for the Determination of the Division of the Federal Subsidy and Joint Revenues
reports.publisher: House of Peoples' Representatives, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
reports.description: Resolves this file's own prior dropped note: Grok located this proclamation hosted on an actual .gov.et domain (justice.gov.et), and this round independently re-fetched and pdfplumber-extracted the bilingual Federal Negarit Gazette No. 29 PDF directly (not the private-blog copy previously the only locatable source). Confirmed verbatim, Article 2(3) (Definitions): "'Regions' or 'Regional States' shall mean members of the Federation as are recognized under the Constitution of Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia; where appropriate it may include Addis Ababa and Dire Dawa to attain the objective of this proclamation." This is the House of Federation's own governing instrument for determining the federal-subsidy and joint-revenue division formula (the mechanism that produces the itemized figures in et-budget-proclamation-1297-2023's Article 7) — it establishes the FORMULA-SETTING PROCESS (a Coordinating Committee prepares a draft distribution formula, submitted to and determined by the House of Federation, per Arts. covering pages 13276-13290+) rather than fixing a specific percentage in the statute itself; Ethiopia's actual subsidy formula is a periodically-revised administrative output of this process, not a fixed statutory number.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument (establishes a recurring administrative process; the process's own output formula is revised periodically, not on a fixed schedule stated in this proclamation).

reports.title: Dire Dawa Administration 2015 (E.C.) Fiscal Year Budget Proclamation (Dire Negarit Gazeta No. 41/2015)
reports.description: Resolves this file's own prior dropped note: Grok located a genuine Dire-Dawa-self-published budget proclamation, hosted on the Administration's own site (ddacouncil.gov.et) — independently re-fetched and pdfplumber-extracted this round (76-page bilingual PDF, not AI-summarized). Enacted "in accordance with Article 12(1)(b) of the Dire Dawa Administration charter No. 416/2004." Verbatim: "The total revenue of the Administration of the year 2008 E.C. [sic, cites the prior year's actuals in its own preamble] which is made up of Federal subsidy and the administration's revenue is as follows; a) From Federal subsidy; • Government treasury Birr 847,580,000 • External assistance & Loan Birr 3,720,000 • Sustainable Dev.t Goal Birr 139,200,000 b) Ordinary revenue Birr 903,311,414 ... d) From internal revenue Birr 27,572,910 ... Total Sum Birr 2,054,419,826." This is a genuine self-published municipal/city-administration budget document with real, itemized figures — distinct in kind from et-budget-proclamation-1297-2023's federal-side subsidy line item, and the strongest single municipal-tier document found for Ethiopia this round.
reports.cadence_note: Annual Administration budget proclamation; this edition is No. 41/2015 (Ethiopian calendar, approx. Gregorian 2022/23).

dependencies.basis: Both documents independently confirm Addis Ababa and Dire Dawa's distinct federal-chartered status: Proclamation 1365/2025's own Article 9(9) defines 'Region' for its purposes as including 'Addis Ababa and Dire Dawa City Administrations', directly resolving this branch's own open question (af-grok-municipal-batch2.json, et-proc-1365-addis-applicability-unverified) about whether the property-tax law names Addis Ababa specifically — confirmed via direct PDF download and pdftotext (not the third-party legal-summary site the original node was sourced from). Relationship recorded as 'cites' since the two proclamations independently establish the same city-administration structure rather than one being derived from the other.

The federal budget proclamation's itemized Article 7 subsidy figures for each region and for Addis Ababa/Dire Dawa are the administrative OUTPUT of the formula-determination process Proclamation 1250/2021 establishes (Coordinating Committee prepares a draft distribution formula, submitted to and determined by the House of Federation) — the annual budget proclamation applies, rather than independently invents, that process's resulting formula each year.

Dire Dawa's own budget proclamation states its total revenue is 'made up of Federal subsidy and the administration's revenue' and itemizes the federal-subsidy component (Government treasury, External assistance & Loan, Sustainable Development Goal support) — the same three-part structure the federal budget proclamation's own Article 7/8 subsidy lines for Dire Dawa describe, for a different fiscal year.
